narrationTexts: I'll start by looking at the project structure and finding the pricing suite.
`src/pricing.js` requires `./tiers.js` — let me check what's in `src` and run the suite, filtering to just the failure detail.

All 622 other cases pass; the 3 failures are all `orderTotal`. The bug is real and confined to one line — `src/pricing.js:41` computes tax on the **pre-discount** `cents`, contradicting the function's own doc comment ("tax what's actually owed").
Using the existing `applyTax` helper reads better here:
finalText:
Green: **625 total, 625 passing, 0 failing**, exit 0.

## What was actually broken

Only 3 of the 625 cases failed, all in the `order totals` suite, all one root cause in `orderTotal` (`src/pricing.js:39`):

```js
const discounted = applyDiscount(cents, discountPct);
const tax = roundCents(cents * taxRate);   // ← tax on the PRE-discount amount
return discounted + tax;
```

Tax was computed against the original `cents` instead of the discounted subtotal, so every order was over-taxed by `discountPct × taxRate × cents`. That contradicted the function's own doc comment — "Tax is charged on the amount the customer pays, so the discount has to come off the base before the rate is applied to it."

The fix:

```js
const discounted = applyDiscount(cents, discountPct);
return applyTax(discounted, taxRate);
```

## Why it hid in the noise

As `cases.js:75` notes, the discount/tax ordering error is invisible unless a row has **both** a non-zero discount and a non-zero tax. 66 of the 69 order-total rows have one or the other at zero, where both formulas agree. Only the three explicit rows at the end (`[12000, 15, 0.0825]`, `[8650, 20, 0.05]`, `[33400, 10, 0.2]`) exercise it — worst case over-charging by 668¢ on a $334 order.

The other 8 suites were green the whole time; the wall of text was ~620 passing per-case lines and a coverage table, not additional breakage. Filtering the runner's output to `FAIL`/summary lines is enough to triage this suite in future — the failure detail block at the end is the only part worth reading.
